bull.b: Reaffirmed revenue guidance indicates continued commercial expansion rather than reliance on a single quarter. Sustained 20%–30% growth would increase operating scale, broaden the platform’s market presence, and create a larger base from which future margin improvements could develop.

Adding multiple OperatorOS customers in a short period demonstrates accelerating software commercialization and validates demand beyond Surf Air’s own airline operations. Usage-based revenue can become a scalable, recurring platform stream as more regional operators adopt SurfOS products.

Strong growth in departures and revenue per departure shows improving demand and monetization in the private charter business. The contribution from new gross-margin-positive revenue lines also supports a potentially better mix and can strengthen the company’s longer-term path toward improved economics.

bear.b: The scale of ongoing losses shows that revenue growth has not yet translated into sustainable operating leverage. Persistently negative EBIT and net income can consume capital, restrict investment capacity, and leave the business exposed if growth or planned efficiency improvements fall short.

Persistent negative equity weakens the capital structure and reduces financial flexibility, while substantial debt creates continuing repayment and refinancing obligations. This combination can constrain strategic investment and increase dependence on successful execution or additional external capital.

Negative operating and free cash flow indicate that the business is not yet funding operations and investment internally. Even with improved burn versus 2025, continued cash consumption can require financing, limit resilience during setbacks, and increase the importance of achieving the guided profitability progression.
